problem: The storage package is intended to define repository ports, but it also owns SQLite/SQLAlchemy implementations, environment-aware database settings and provider construction. Those concrete responsibilities import persistence, observability and runtime, reverse the dependency direction and keep storage inside the core SCC.

options.name: Keep concrete providers in storage
options.correctness: Preserves current imports but retains the 7-package SCC and makes the abstraction package depend on its implementations.

options.name: Move provider implementation and construction into persistence
options.correctness: Keeps storage repository contracts unchanged while making persistence the sole concrete implementation owner and updating every in-repository caller to the new explicit surface.
options.complexity: A bounded ownership migration across provider files and import-only callers.
options.migration: Move settings, factory and SQLAlchemy provider to persistence; update callers and migrations; delete old storage implementations; run full verification.
options.rollback: Restore the three storage implementation files and previous imports.
options.verification: Boundary/SCC counterexample, transaction storage tests, migration imports, full Quick, lifecycle and Chromium.

options.name: Keep old storage imports through a dynamic facade
options.correctness: Could hide static dependency edges but would retain a runtime Service Locator and two apparent ownership surfaces.
options.migration: Use importlib or __getattr__ to forward storage imports to persistence.
options.verification: Static graph would improve without a true ownership cutover.

rejected_reasons.keep-concrete-providers-in-storage: It preserves the wrong abstraction-to-implementation dependency direction.
rejected_reasons.dynamic-storage-compatibility-facade: It would manufacture apparent graph improvement while preserving hidden runtime coupling and ambiguous ownership.

deletions: Delete storage.factory, storage.settings and storage.sqlalchemy_provider after their single implementations move to persistence; delete all repository references to those old import paths.
unknowns: The remaining 6-package SCC remains open debt.
State/Loop simplification and real-model certification remain separate future targets.
selected_responsibilities: agent_core.storage owns repository protocols, transaction scopes and persistence value contracts only.
agent_core.persistence owns SQLite/SQLAlchemy implementations, database settings and StoreProvider construction.
Application, transaction, observability and migration callers consume the persistence implementation surface explicitly.
preserved_hard_invariants: StoreProvider and all repository protocols remain unchanged.
Database tables, migration semantics, transaction state and idempotency behavior remain unchanged.
context, modules, kernel, resources, ledger, rag and utils remain outside the main SCC.
The dependency debt baseline is not edited.
cutover_strategy: Record expected-red, move the three concrete storage responsibilities to persistence without logic changes, update all callers and migration imports, delete old implementation owners, then run complete product verification.
acceptance_claims: storage imports no persistence, observability or runtime package and contains no concrete provider implementation.
persistence contains the sole provider/settings/SQLAlchemy implementations and all callers use them.
The current SCC member count is at most 6 and storage plus all prior removed packages remain outside it.
All transaction, migration, lifecycle, frontend and browser tests remain green.
